GWDD Model Verification Dashboard

U.S. Gas-Weighted Degree Day forecasts — GFS · ECE · GEFS · vs. observed history

Model Scorecard

Summary stats per model × lead-time window. Cells are tinted green (better than peers in the same window) to red (worse).

Forecast vs Actual

Time series of mean forecast within the selected lead-time window, overlaid on observed GWDD with a ±1 GWDD band.

Bias & Seasonality

Mean (forecast − actual). Positive = model forecasts higher GWDD than realized (cold bias on demand). Bars with |bias| > 1 GWDD are red-bordered.

Model Convergence

Average RMSE by lead day. Error typically grows as the lead time extends.

Forecast Revisions

Mean absolute run-over-run change. Higher = more volatile guidance; lower = more stable.

Model Divergence (GFS vs ECE)

Rolling 30-day average of |GFS − ECE| spread per ForecastDate, by window. Wider spread = more model disagreement.

Regime Performance

Lower bars = better forecasts. MAE expressed as a percentage of the mean observed GWDD in that regime, so cold/normal/warm groups are directly comparable despite their very different absolute magnitudes. Regimes are terciles of observed GWDD: Cold ≤ 9.12 (summer baseline), Normal 9.12–15.84 (shoulder), Warm > 15.84 (winter peak demand). The dashed line marks 15% — a rough "weak forecast" threshold; bars above it are unreliable.

Lead-Day Sanity Check

All forecast stats broken out by integer lead day, including lead 0 (nowcast — same-day "diagnosis") and lead 15 (longest horizon). Lead 0 should be near-perfect (model's own initialization); lead 15 should be the worst. Anything that breaks that pattern is a data issue worth investigating.

Bias by GWDD Magnitude

Mean Bias (forecast − actual) and MAE binned by the magnitude of the observed actual GWDD. Tells you whether models systematically under- or over-shoot when actuals are small vs. large. A 15-GWDD miss when the actual was 35 (winter peak) is a different story than a 15-GWDD miss when the actual was 10 (shoulder).

KDCA — ECE Forecast Bias on Extreme Events

Single-station ECE 51-member ensemble (00Z, 6-hour steps, 2020–2025) for Reagan National (KDCA). Temperatures converted °C→°F, then HDD = max(0, 65 − TF) and CDD = max(0, TF − 65). Lead 0 (the same-day "nowcast") serves as the observed proxy. Bias = forecastL − actual0: NEGATIVE bias = model UNDER-predicted (forecast was warmer than reality → missed the cold for HDD, or cooler than reality → missed the heat for CDD). POSITIVE bias = model OVER-predicted (cold bias for HDD, hot bias for CDD). The interesting question: does the bias get worse on the days that actually matter — the coldest winter and hottest summer days?

Bias Evolution by Lead Day

Mean forecast bias by lead day (forecast − actual), split by category. Negative = model under-predicted (missed the cold/heat). Positive = model over-predicted (cold bias for HDD, hot bias for CDD). Watch the spread between the "all" and "extreme" lines — that's how much extra bias the model carries on the high-impact days.

Top Extreme Events — Forecast Evolution

Top 25 events per category, showing how the forecast for that day looked at leads 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 14 vs. the lead-0 realization. Bias columns = forecast − actual (negative = model under-predicted the extreme).

Extreme Events

Granular row-level lookups — three sections: (1) most extreme forecasts (standardized anomaly, z-scored by month), (2) most extreme observed actuals (top & bottom of the history), (3) biggest forecast misses per individual lead day 10–15.

Most Extreme Forecasts (top 50 by |z|)

Anomaly standardized by month-of-year std-dev so summer/winter are comparable. Higher |z| = more unusual call.

Most Extreme Observed Actuals

Top 15 highest and 15 lowest GWDD days in the history file.

Biggest Misses — Per Lead Day 10–15

Top 10 largest |Error| rows for the selected lead day. Drill into specific events.
